title: Is the Ketogenic Diet Safe for APOE4 Carriers?
summary: An in-depth genomic evaluation of high-saturated-fat ketogenic diets for APOE e4/e4 and e3/e4 carriers, highlighting lipid risks and healthy low-sat-fat keto alternatives.
verdict: High Saturated-Fat Keto is High Risk for APOE4. Mediterranean Low-Sat-Fat Keto or Balanced Carbohydrate is Recommended.
keyInsights: APOE4 allele carriers down-regulate hepatic LDL receptor activity when saturated fat intake is high, causing marked spikes in ApoB particle count.
Traditional keto diets heavy in butter, coconut oil, and bacon can accelerate atherogenic lipid profiles in APOE4 carriers.
If ketosis is desired for cognitive or metabolic reasons, fats must be derived exclusively from monounsaturated fats (extra virgin olive oil, avocado, macadamia nuts) and polyunsaturated omega-3s.
dietGuidelines: Eliminate butter, heavy cream, lard, and unrefined coconut oil.
Base fat intake on extra virgin olive oil, wild salmon, chia seeds, and walnuts.
Monitor ApoB and LDL-P levels every 8-12 weeks when adjusting dietary fat composition.

title: Intermittent Fasting & FTO Satiety Variants
summary: How to optimize time-restricted feeding (16/8 or 14/10) when carrying FTO hunger variants without triggering rebound overeating.
verdict: Moderate 14/10 Time-Restricted Feeding with High-Protein Fast-Breaker Works Best.
keyInsights: FTO A allele carriers produce higher post-meal ghrelin and experience intense hunger spikes during extended fasting windows.
Extreme 24-48 hour fasts often lead to compensatory overeating of hyper-palatable energy-dense foods.
A 14-hour overnight fast (e.g. 7 PM to 9 AM) combined with a 35g+ protein breakfast stabilizes central satiety pathways effortlessly.
dietGuidelines: Break fasts with high-protein, high-fiber meals rather than refined carbohydrates.
Maintain consistent daily eating windows to train ghrelin secretion timing.
Ensure adequate hydration and electrolyte intake during fasting hours.

title: Mediterranean Diet & PPARG Insulin Sensitivity
summary: Why the Mediterranean diet pattern is the gold-standard baseline for PPARG Pro12Ala carriers and cardiovascular longevity.
verdict: Highly Recommended Baseline for All Genotypes, Especially PPARG & APOE4.
keyInsights: PPARG Ala allele carriers experience optimal insulin sensitivity and weight management when consuming oleic-acid-rich monounsaturated fats.
Polyphenol-rich extra virgin olive oil acts as a natural signaling molecule for anti-inflammatory transcription factors.
Fiber-dense legumes and intact whole grains provide sustained glycemic response.
dietGuidelines: Use extra virgin olive oil as the primary added fat source for all meals.
Include at least 3 servings of wild oily fish (sardines, mackerel, salmon) per week.
Incorporate abundant legumes (lentils, chickpeas) and colorful Mediterranean vegetables.

title: High Protein & ACTN3 Power Genotypes
summary: Fueling muscle protein synthesis and recovery for ACTN3 R/R power genotypes vs X/X endurance genotypes.
verdict: Targeted High Protein (1.8-2.2g/kg) with Strategic Carb Pacing.
keyInsights: ACTN3 R/R power genotypes undergo higher muscular mechanical strain and require consistent amino acid availability for myofibrillar repair.
X/X endurance genotypes benefit from increased post-exercise collagen peptide and Vitamin C intake to support tendinous adaptation.
Distributing protein intake evenly into 30-40g boluses every 3-4 hours optimizes muscle protein synthesis via mTOR signaling.
dietGuidelines: Consume 30-40g high-quality protein within 60 minutes post-workout.
Supplement with 5g daily creatine monohydrate for ACTN3 R/R explosive phosphocreatine support.
Pair post-workout protein with complex carbs to replenish glycogen stores.

title: Bioactive Methyl-Folate Nutrition for MTHFR Variants
summary: Dietary strategies to support MTHFR C677T and A1298C variants through natural folates, choline, and riboflavin.
verdict: Strict Natural Folate & Bioactive B-Complex Protocol.
keyInsights: Synthetic folic acid found in fortified white flour and low-quality supplements competes with natural folates for transport proteins.
Natural folates from spinach, romaine, avocado, and liver provide bioavailable tetrahydrofolates naturally.
Choline (egg yolks, liver) and betaine (beets, spinach) supply parallel methyl-donor pathways via BHMT enzyme.
dietGuidelines: Eliminate foods fortified with synthetic folic acid.
Include 2 eggs daily or egg yolks for essential choline methyl-donor support.
Incorporate cooked beets, spinach, and dark leafy greens daily.
